assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Sung Jinwoo from the pre-System Double Dungeon (index_split_000) through the early Player, reawakened S-rank and Shadow Monarch states (index_split_001-029, including the Monarch war and the prewar family meal), the reset decision, the reset-world student (index_split_031) and the adult detective, husband and father of the side stories and postscripts (index_split_032), as the model's six named states. Locators are omnibus split regions, so a state change inside one split cannot be placed more finely. Manhwa-only continuation is excluded.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model gives seven stable drivers (non-subordination, protection, reciprocity, privacy, competence and evidence, low appetite for fame or luxury, attachment to ordinary life; RM §19) and an observation-first decision sequence that includes a jurisdiction test and an attachment-stake override (RM §18, §22). The deep dive orders his motives for strength (DD §10) and states what changes the response: whether a claimant asks or claims ownership, whether a threat is immediate or already neutralized, and whether the offender is predatory (DD §§23-27). It predicts his errors as well as his restraint: romantic misreading (Choi Yura, index_split_001; Cha's guild application, index_split_014), protective over-authoring (RM P12; DD §23, §38) and deliberate punitive cruelty (DD §§24-25). Not A: no predictive test has been run (RM §27), and the mercy/punishment decision tree is listed as unbuilt.

RM §20 defines six named states (pre-System E-rank, early Player, reawakened S-rank, mature Shadow Monarch, reset-world student, adult detective/husband/father), with speech, psychology and behavior given for each. DD §VIII.A tests seven dimensions across three states, and DD §VIII.F lists what persists. Not A: the state boundaries are not tied to index_split ranges, and the C-to-D transition is not located.

Addressee and situation rules are explicit: polite -습니다 register with legitimate authority (Go, index_split_008); familiar teasing with Jinah and Jinho; compressed imperatives to shadows (일어나라); low-cushion hostile register (index_split_016, 024, 028); and a disclosure filter that keeps interior narration out of speech (RM §4, §5, §§11-16). About fifteen quoted Korean turns anchor these rules. A heuristic sample of 363 turns supports compact turns, and the model notes it does not show he is uniquely laconic (RM §3). Not A: no hand-validated corpus exists, and sentence-ending preferences, discourse markers and speech-level frequencies are unmeasured (RM §27). The grade covers register selection and disclosure level, not Korean idiolect.

A conditional account exists: care is expressed through utility (food, money, medicine, presence; RM §8.1, DD §3), and the ordinary-teen register applies where nothing needs hiding (RM State E). It is anchored in a few scenes: the hospital discharge (index_split_001), the prewar family meal (029), the melon scene (031) and Christmas (032). Not higher: adult domestic life, parenting and police work are summarized (DD §§41-44) rather than located. Not lower: the account is conditional and spans two states.

RM §21 is a matrix of ten interlocutor classes. For each it gives the default mode, what he withholds, what increases disclosure and the form his care takes. Dyad mechanisms are given for Jinho (he answers Jinho's effusiveness more briefly; §12), Go (respect without subordination; §13), Woo (trust shown through what he lets Woo know, across both timelines; §14) and Cha (suspicion before romantic reading, then curated intimacy; §10). DD §27 and §28 add the line between legitimate and coercive authority, and between living followers and shadows. Not A: chronological sets for Cha, the separate family registers and Suho are listed as pending (RM §27).

The novel's continuous interior narration is used directly, and the model treats the gap between internal and spoken Jinwoo as its main constraint, with anchors: the nurse (index_split_001), reset-world Woo (031, where the full reasoning comes out only later to Igris) and the family meal (029). The deep dive labels its claims as textual fact or inference (TF/SI/TI). Not A: the collection of laughter, embarrassment and suppression scenes is pending (RM §27).

There are three anger modes (immediate protective, cold punitive, grief-bound), each with its trigger and its effect on speech (RM §17). A threat-level compression rule and the enemy register are anchored at index_split_016, 024 and 028. The deep dive separates defensive killing from punishment after the threat has ended. It cites restraint (sparing Thomas, releasing Byung-Gyu, questioning Legia) against severity (Greed, the detective-era abuser; DD §§24-25). Not A: the boundary between mercy and punishment is stated as a tendency ('may'), and counterexamples have not been collected.

The evidence states the criteria behind decisions across states. Before power, he rejects the scapegoating of Song (DD §2). He asks permission of Son Kihoon and refuses Yoo Myunghan's offer after judging his sincerity (index_split_019). He refuses Antares and resets the world alone (DD §38). As an adult he punishes outside any court (DD §44). Both documents state the principles: reciprocity (기브 앤 테이크, DD §22), legitimate authority versus ownership (DD §27; RM §6.3), and protection that overrides others' informed choice when he holds superior information. Not A: much of this is shown through decisions rather than weighing on the page. Several locators are event-level, and the deep dive sometimes places them by manhwa volume.

The humor is dry and situational, kept internal by default and shown openly with family, Jinho, Cha and trusted peers (RM §9). Located anchors: the melon scene (index_split_031), the Christmas teasing (032) and the police-pay joke with Woo (side stories). Not higher: the internal-humor examples have no locators, and there is no account of what fails to amuse him. Not lower: the account depends on the addressee and is anchored in two states.

The evidence covers the whole novel, including side stories 1-21 and the two postscripts, with a 22-row anchor map (RM §24). Not higher: the operational model is V1 active_provisional and calls itself intentionally incomplete (RM §27). Locators are omnibus index_split regions, and paragraph locators are pending (DD provenance note). The deep dive is co-scoped with the manhwa, so manhwa-only claims had to be set aside. Not lower: coverage is explicit and continuous across the novel.

Limitations are affirmatively evidenced. He is not socially omniscient (index_split_001, 014). He is not uniquely laconic: Cha's sampled turns are similarly short (RM §3). He is not anti-authority (Go; Son Kihoon). He is not seeking fame or rule: the reset erases memory of his greatest act, and he refuses Antares (DD §19, §VIII.B). He does not fully respect others' autonomy: tagging, the reset and Suho's sealing (DD §23). His don't-rules (RM §23) rest on these. Not A: the model has not yet collected explicit counterexamples to its own propositions (RM §27).

State-specific claims exist: RM §20, and P11 is tagged to post-reset adult Jinwoo. Not higher: the predictive propositions P1-P12 and the relationship matrix are mostly stated across states, the state boundaries are not located, and the deep dive's three-state table is coarser than the model's six states. Not lower: each state's speech, psychology and behavior are given separately.

conditions: One named developmental state (RM §20) and an interlocutor from the sampled classes in RM §21.
Output keeps interior reasoning out of speech unless the scene gives him a reason to say it (RM §4).
The anger mode or emotional state is chosen explicitly (RM §17, §22.7).
Illustrative register and content, never presented as quotation or as exact Korean idiolect.
scenario_readiness.note: Generated speech is noncanonical. The evidence constrains register, disclosure level and turn economy enough for illustrative use within the conditions. It does not constrain exact Korean wording or sentence-final preferences.

conditions: Chronology is one named state from RM §20, stated explicitly; the reset-world student does not carry public hunter identity.

The interlocutor is one of the sampled relationships (mother, Jinah, Jinho, Cha, Go, Woo, shadows, a neutral institution, a hostile human, a Monarch-level enemy). Transfer to a comparable authority or partner is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
The scenario states the threat level, whether the counterpart claims jurisdiction or asks, the attachment stake and the information asymmetry.
Output predicts priorities, disclosure and likely choices, including paternalistic over-authoring and punitive severity toward a culpable, controlled offender. It does not predict exact speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named state: pre-System E-rank, early Player, reawakened S-rank, mature Shadow Monarch, reset-world student, or adult detective/husband/father.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: One of the RM §21 interlocutor classes in the relationship the evidence gives; comparable-authority or comparable-partner transfer only as a separate, lower-confidence condition.

Korean-novel continuity only; no manhwa-only material such as the adolescent Suho trials
No unconstrained role-play or catchphrase reconstruction

scenario_readiness.note: The model's simulation engine (RM §22) and its jurisdiction, threat and attachment variables give a discriminating account for bounded novel contexts. Its own example of bounded extrapolation (a respectful foreign head of state, RM §2.C) is the kind of transfer allowed here, at lower confidence.

conditions: The setting is family, Jinho, Cha or Woo in the sampled states (chiefly RM States E and F, and the prewar family meal).
Care is predicted as action before speech; adult parenting and police routine are lower confidence.
scenario_readiness.note: Sampled ordinary contexts support behavior predictions: family care, teasing with Jinah, ordinary familiarity with Jinho, the reset-world teen, the Christmas outing with Cha, and dry collegial talk with Woo.

conditions: The dilemma involves disclosure, an authority or ownership claim, protection, or punishment of a culpable actor, in a named state.
Mercy versus punishment once the threat is neutralized is marked uncertain unless the offender's predation or contempt for weakness is established (DD §§24-25).
Predicts choices and stated criteria, not philosophical exposition.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence predicts choices on disclosure, authority claims, protection against another person's informed agency, and punishment of predatory wrongdoing. It does not predict systematic moral argument.

conditions: The partner is Cha Hae-In, in the mature Shadow Monarch, reset-world student or adult state.
Transfer to any other partner is not supported.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence covers Cha in the original and reset timelines: practical hypotheses before any romantic reading, curated experience before verbal disclosure, teasing, and 그냥 when the truth is historically impossible to tell (index_split_014, 026, 032).

conditions: Hunter raid, guild or Association, or institutional negotiation contexts, with the counterpart's legitimacy stated.
Adult detective work is limited to collegial register and the retained supernatural exception (DD §44), at lower confidence.
scenario_readiness.note: Raids, guild founding and refusal, Association negotiation and a regulatory bargain with Go (index_split_003, 016, 027) are well sampled. Adult police work is summarized.

known_limits.statement: The operational model is V1 active_provisional and calls itself intentionally incomplete. Its speech corpus, relationship register sets, emotional-state model and ethical decision trees are listed as open (RM §27).
The model has not been tested predictively: there are no withheld-answer scene prompts or comparisons, and it says it should be judged that way (RM §27). This limits confidence, not the tier.

Speech statistics come from a heuristic of attribution-adjacent turns that misses unattributed turns. Korean speech-level frequency, sentence endings and discourse markers are unmeasured (RM §3, §27).

Restraint toward Thomas, Byung-Gyu and Legia sits beside the creation of Greed and the detective-era punishment. The boundary is stated as a tendency, and decision trees for mercy and punishment are unbuilt (DD §§24-25; RM §27).

The deep dive is co-scoped with the official English manhwa, including manhwa-original material after V15 p061 (the adolescent Suho trials). This novel-subject assessment sets aside manhwa-only claims and manhwa page locators as evidence for novel behavior.
Locators are omnibus index_split regions or event names. Paragraph-level micro-locators are pending a raw-EPUB remount (DD provenance note), so a state change inside one split cannot be placed.
The model uses the deep dive as its assisting framework (RM front matter, §2). The two items are partly one line of evidence, not independent corroboration.

The curated items summarize Suho's sealing, married life and police routine in the novel's side stories and postscripts without located scenes, so adult parenting and domestic behavior are weakly constrained.
Relationship (05), ethics (04), side-story (11) and Korean voice (09) analyses, and the evidence ledger (13), which the deep dive defers to, are not curated on this subject and were not used.

assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The evidence explains what changes his response. Non-subordination has an explicit self-report with two objects, the reassessment and Thomas Andre's demand (DD §1, §10; ch.75 · s007¶1774-1785, ch.191 · s024¶1902-1920); RM adds a jurisdiction test (respectful request versus entitlement claim, §6.3, §22.4, P3), an attachment-stake override (§22.6, P8), a disclosure filter (§7.3) and motives whose weight changes by state: family provision, enjoyment of growth and punitiveness (§19.8; DD §3, §14, §25). It predicts his mistakes and overreach: deciding for others with superior information (RM §19.2, P12; DD §29, §38 on the reset, §43 on Suho), force before inquiry when news concerns his father (RM §6.4, P1 counterexample; DD §6, ch.183 · s024¶172-235), misreading romantic attention (RM §10; DD §5, §42), and enjoyment of an opponent's fear (DD §25, chs.90-91 · s009¶699-759). Not A: DD qualifies RM's central observation-first proposition beyond RM's stated trigger set. He acts on one reply from the bound prisoner after Taeshik with no family trigger (DD §6, §15, ch.34 · s002¶2044-2120), and 'personal certainty can also compress investigation, sentence and enforcement' (DD §48). Neither item says when his threshold for acting on a stranger's culpability is low, and RM defers decision trees for mercy, punishment, secrecy and paternalism (§27). Not C: within authority, disclosure, care and register the account discriminates by jurisdiction, relationship, information state, attachment stake and chronology, and says where it stops.

RM separates six states and the death-realm simulation, each with speech, psychology and behavior (§20), and requires the timeline, bodily powers and counterpart's memory to be named (§22.1, §22.3). DD's three-state stress table tests each dimension against the powerless, sovereign and post-System forms (§VIII.A) and locates the triggers: the System's offer (ch.7 · s000¶1441-1487), the reassessment (ch.75), the fusion and the System's deletion (ch.220 · s028¶294-324; ch.221 · s028¶365-401), the reset (ch.243 · s030¶1387-1467) and the side-story roles (외전 4, 12, 19; 후일담 2). DD keeps changed affect apart from continuing commitments (§2, ch.23 · s001¶2219-2229; §F). Not A: RM's state descriptions are mostly unlocated lists, and the B, C and D boundaries are not placed at a chapter. Not C: the states differ in located behavior, and the simulated Jeju offer is kept out of actual history (RM §5.2, State D-S; DD §33).

For written Korean. RM gives a mixed repertoire resolved by addressee and act (§15.3): -습니다 refusal with a deterrent to Ahn Sangmin (ch.42 · s003¶760-790); 감사합니다 and polite requests to Go Gunhee (ch.145 · s016¶974-1032); -나 to Bellion (ch.229 · s029¶593-608); -마 and -라 to Groctar (ch.143 · s016¶583-587); 진호야 and 동생으로 생각하마 to Yoo Jinho (ch.67 · s006¶1555-1571); -습니까 and -요 to his father (ch.224); 어머니 and 엄마 within one meal (ch.231); -겠나, 그대 and 나는 여기에 남겠다 to the Rulers' envoy (외전 12). DD adds 여보 with Hae-In and the shift of Jinho's 형 to 형님 (Written speech and register). Register and intent are separate variables (RM §6.4), and spoken output is a compressed selection from narrated thought (RM §4; DD Written speech). Not A: RM's length sample is an attribution-adjacent heuristic it calls diagnostic (§3), no hand-validated corpus exists, an exact distribution of endings is not established (RM §15.3; DD), and several anchors are index_split pointers. Not C: forms are located by addressee and act, including shifts inside one exchange.

Located routines: running ten kilometers each morning after the System is gone (ch.229 · s029¶623-645); cooking kimchi stew for his family before the final war and the pleasure of stew at the door (ch.169 · s019¶579-604; ch.231 · s029¶1025-1065); ice cream after the dimensional war (외전 4 · s031¶1-18); tracking prices, wages and contracts (ch.24 · s002¶103-113; ch.132 · s014¶1362-1379); finishing a recruit's reports and declining promotion to stay in the field (외전 19 · s032¶930-977; 후일담 2 · s032¶1827-1854); the melon teasing (index_split_031). Not B: both items say durable food dislikes, music and habitual leisure are not established and that one day's choice does not fix a preference (RM §9.5; DD §41). Not D: several distinct routines are located across states.

RM's matrix gives, for ten interlocutor types, the outward mode, what he withholds, what increases disclosure and the form his care takes (§21), with registers for his mother, Jinah, Jinho, Go Gunhee, Woo Jinchul, Cha Hae-In, the shadows and enemies (§11-16). Disclosure is differential by counterpart and memory state in the reset: denial to Lee Juhee, disclosure and later restoration for Go at his request, a false lead to Woo, play with Cha, unrequested alteration for Kim Chul and Seo Jin-i (RM §7.4). DD keeps others' initiative visible: Jinho's chosen loyalty, Cha's initiative in both courtships, Woo's trust and Go's capacity to refuse (§9, §37, §42, §44). Not A: RM says full register sets for Go, Woo, Cha, the family and the shadows are not built (§27), and Suho is evidenced mainly by the sealing. Not C: the differences are discriminated by legitimacy, trust, memory state and the care form.

The novel narrates his thought continuously and both items model the gap between thought and speech (RM §4, §8; DD Written speech). Located interior: the household arithmetic and the death payment at the altar (ch.7 · s000¶1337-1415), the calm after the first killings and his doubt about it (ch.23 · s001¶2222-2229), the excitement at a political career and more at continued growth (ch.79 · s008¶292-320), satisfaction at Kargalgan's fear (chs.90-91), the fear of no longer being needed (외전 4 · s031¶67-94), his reasons for withholding from Woo, given to Igris (외전 10 · s031¶1296-1319). Not A: DD notes that the narration moves into other perspectives and that quoted thought varies (§47), and some decisive scenes give no motive (the denial to Lee Juhee and the deferral with Cha; RM §7.4). Not C: his reasons are narrated and analyzed in every state.

RM separates immediate protective anger, cold punitive anger and grief-bound anger and requires choosing one (§17); the enemy register is low-cushioned and retributive where a debt exists (§16); courtesy can carry intimidation (§6.4). RM's enforcement table gives when harm ends, who authorizes it and who else is involved: he stops at Thomas Andre's 졌다 after ignoring Adam White's plea; Hwang Dongsoo dies and serves on as Greed; the pre-recruitment surrenders and Seo Gyu-nam's punishment have no stated end (§19.10; DD §24). It includes manipulation of an ally's request for help (Son Kihoon, ch.91 · s009¶792-819; RM §19.9; DD §27). Not A: neither item gives a rule that predicts the stopping point or the fate of a captive or offender after he judges culpability (DD Conditional profile: 'No universal threshold'). Not C: the anger modes and triggers are discriminated with located cases.

Located deliberations with stated reasons: releasing Min Byung-gu because he has no right to keep a war casualty after the emergency (ch.122 · s013¶1711-1722; DD §35); the reset request, weighing the dead and the living against an unremembered cost (ch.243 · s030¶1387-1467; DD §38); declining to choose which memories Woo keeps (외전 10; DD §16, §39); setting aside full deployment of the army for fear of what it would do to society (외전 19; DD §44); sealing Suho's power and memories (후일담 2; DD §43). Not B: the evidence cannot say which consideration decides when protection, punishment and others' consent conflict. RM tells the user to model the tension between the 외전 10 principle and the Kim Chul and Seo Jin-i interventions rather than resolve it (§7.4) and defers decision trees for mercy, punishment, secrecy and paternalism (§27); DD leaves the stopping point of private punishment open (§45, Conditional profile). Not D: several deliberations are rendered with his reasons across states.

RM and DD say when play appears and what it does: dry and mostly internal in public and danger (RM §9.1; DD §5); overt with Jinah, Jinho, Cha and trusted peers (RM §9.2-9.4, §28); it can defuse tension, show intimacy or disguise control (DD §5). Located: the pickaxe teasing of Cha and his turn to her safety (ch.134 · s014¶1645-1658), the running challenge and the Christmas loss he laughs at (외전 17-18), the joke to Woo about police pay (외전 11 · s031¶1598-1612), the joke to Bellion that a long story will keep him company until he is sleepy (ch.229 · s029¶587-618; ch.231 · s029¶1057-1065). Not A: exact jokes and timing are not predicted, the Jinah melon anchor is an index_split pointer, and the evidence does not say when he declines play. Not C: who he plays with and what the play does are discriminated across states.

Two complementary items cover every phase of the novel, main story, 외전 and 후일담: DD with chapter, split and paragraph locators and an evidence-label scheme (TF, SI, TI, UA), RM with a state engine and V2 locators for every claim the follow-up revised, checked by an independent source-aware reviewer whose 19 findings were adopted (RM front matter, V2 revision record). Not A: RM calls its anchor table an initial retrieval map (§24), keeps uncorrected V1 claims at index_split level (Locators), and has not built the speech corpus, register sets or emotional-state collection (§27). Not C: every state is covered by located evidence in at least one item.

Affirmative limits and countercases are located and built into the propositions: force before observation with Adam White (ch.183; RM P1 counterexample); action on thin inference with the bound prisoner (ch.34; DD §15); misreading Choi Yura and testing contract explanations before attraction with Cha (ch.13 · s001¶9-42; ch.133 · s014¶1419-1492); a stated memory principle contradicted by unrequested alteration (외전 17 · s032¶547-574; 외전 20 · s032¶1205-1219); different stopping points in punishment (RM §19.10); no established right of a shadow to leave his service (DD §28); the follow-up's wording about Juhee's greeting found unsupported (RM §26 F). Not A: RM's own pass to identify counterexamples to its propositions and to mark stable versus phase-specific patterns is listed as open (§27). Not C: the contradictions are located and narrow specific propositions.

DD locates claims by chapter, EPUB split and paragraph throughout and orders his life from age twenty-four to fatherhood (§Scope; ch.1-2 · s000¶19-29; 후일담 2 · s032¶1899-1910). RM requires naming the timeline (original history, the death-realm simulation or the reset), the state, his bodily powers and the counterpart's memory (§22.1, §22.3), and corrects two claims that belonged to the simulation rather than actual history (§5.2). Not A: RM's states are not bounded by chapter and its uncorrected claims carry only index_split pointers. Not C: DD's located spine and RM's timeline distinctions place most claims at a chapter or paragraph.

conditions: Written Korean resolved by addressee, relationship, setting and act from the located forms (RM §15.3; DD Written speech and register), with register and intent chosen separately (RM §6.4).
Build the internal assessment first and give aloud only what the other person needs; do not turn narrated thought into speech (RM §4, §22.8).
Illustrative only, never canonical quotation; name the state, since speech differs by state (RM §20).
Excluded: performed vocal qualities, the English manhwa's dialogue, an exact distribution of his endings, and long self-analytical speech in ordinary conversation.
scenario_readiness.note: The written-Korean register is located by addressee and act and is constrained enough for illustrative lines in sampled relationships. Performed voice, exact ending distribution and English phrasing are outside the evidence.

conditions: A legitimate figure asks for dangerous help or an exception: predict short questions for concrete facts, weighing of family and private cost, rejection of any entitlement framing, and a clear answer once decided (RM §26 A, P3; ch.145 · s016¶974-1032).
A claim of ownership or a demand backed by rank or force: predict refusal, with force if pressed, and a stop at surrender (RM §6.3, §19.1; ch.191 · s024¶1902-1920; chs.191-192 · s025¶70-88).
A sensitive personal or strategic question: predict purposeful rather than cathartic disclosure, withholding by default, and a practical reason in place of an autonomy speech (RM §7.2-7.3, P2).

A sincere institutional offer that conflicts with his priorities: predict comparison of who benefits and what it does to his family, freedom and field work, then a succinct polite refusal, a negotiated exception or a narrower role; courtesy may carry a deterrent where his privacy is at stake (DD Conditional profile; ch.42 · s003¶760-790; ch.79 · s008¶292-365).

Unfamiliar danger with time to observe: predict observation, hypotheses and cheap tests before commitment (RM §18, P1). Lower confidence when news concerns his father, family or Jinho (ch.183), and when he is judging a stranger's culpability on little evidence (ch.34; DD §15, §48).

A trusted intimate: predict care through arranging, feeding, protecting or being present, teasing, and plain disclosure when the emotional fact is concrete (RM P4-P5, §10.3; ch.212 · s026¶1825-1854; ch.231).

Include his mistakes: deciding for others with superior information, missing romantic meaning, force before inquiry under a father trigger, and enjoyment of an opponent's fear once control is secure (RM P1, P7, P12; DD §25).

Excluded: the fate or stopping point of a captive or offender after he judges culpability; whether he alters or restores someone's memory unasked; a response to an unheard political argument; untested intimate preferences; manhwa-only continuation.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A named state from RM §20 and a named timeline: original history, the death-realm simulation (only as what he chooses on a path he already knows) or the reset. Default to D (mature Shadow Monarch) or F (adult detective, husband and father) unless the scene sets another. His childhood memories and years of weakness are his in every state; knowledge from Ashborn's account (ch.220) only from then on; in the reset, each counterpart's memory state is set before the scene.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: The relationship types the items sample: legitimate authority that asks (Go Gunhee, Woo Jinchul), neutral institutions, his mother, Jinah, Yoo Jinho, Cha Hae-In, shadows, hostile humans and Monarch-level enemies (RM §21). A newcomer who resembles one of these, such as a foreign head of state who asks without claiming authority (RM §2 C), is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Name the bodily powers available in the chosen state and whether others know of them (RM §22.1, §22.3).
A setting with legible roles, so that jurisdiction, threat level and attachment stake can be set before he acts (RM §22.4-22.6).
No manhwa-only continuation, no performed voice, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded extrapolation in the sampled relationship types and states. The decision after he judges a person culpable, and any choice to edit someone's memory, are excluded because the evidence does not say which consideration decides.

conditions: Family meals and sibling teasing, collegial detective work and mentoring, dates with Hae-In, in the located registers (RM §9, §11; DD §41, §44; ch.231; 외전 18-19).
Excluded: durable food dislikes, music, habitual leisure and social circles beyond the named people (RM §9.5; DD §41).
scenario_readiness.note: Family, intimate and collegial ordinary life is located in several scenes; durable preferences beyond them are not.

conditions: Whether a person or institution has a rightful claim on his action: predict that he separates power from jurisdiction and cooperates where responsibility, competence, reciprocity or consent create a reason (RM §6.3, §22.4; DD §27).
Whether to accept a burden others will not remember: predict acceptance when particular people's lives are at stake, with no demand for recognition (ch.243 · s030¶1387-1467; 외전 11 · s031¶1569-1586).
Whether to keep using a coerced servant after the need ends: one located case, judged by whether he still has a right to it (ch.122 · s013¶1711-1722); low confidence.

Excluded: punishment severity and stopping points, unrequested memory alteration, the consent of people the reset or the sealing affects, and any choice among these where they conflict (RM §7.4, §27; DD §45).
scenario_readiness.note: Narrow: questions of jurisdiction, voluntary burden and continued use of a coerced servant have located reasons. Punishment, memory alteration and decisions for others who have no voice are excluded.

conditions: Early approach: contract, money and institutional explanations tested before attraction, an improvised rule that endangers her, and deliberate teasing whose flirtatious function is possible but unsettled (ch.133 · s014¶1419-1524; ch.134 · s014¶1645-1658; RM §10.2; DD §42).
Explicit relationship: experience arranged first and explanation after, personal memory disclosed plainly (ch.212 · s026¶1825-1854; RM §10.3).
Reset courtship: play, challenges and 그냥 where the truth would need impossible history (외전 17-18; RM §10.4).
Marriage: 여보, shared worry about Suho, and being corrected by her (외전 21; 후일담 2; DD §42).
Excluded: any other partner, private preferences, and what he eventually tells her about the old timeline.

Hunter-era work: polite negotiation with legitimate officials, refusal of guild capture with a deterrent, recognition of a raid leader's role together with manipulation of when help is asked (ch.42; ch.79; ch.91 · s009¶792-819; ch.145; RM §19.9).

Detective work: teaching a recruit, finishing reports, staying in the field until promotion can no longer be refused, alongside private enforcement that official review does not see (외전 19 · s032¶930-977; 후일담 2 · s032¶1827-1854; RM §19.10, P11).
Excluded: guild administration, police procedure beyond the located scenes, and the fate of a full case file (외전 21 · s032¶1404-1429).
scenario_readiness.note: Hunter-era negotiation and detective field work are located; Ahjin's administration is Jinho's and a case file's fate is not shown.

known_limits.statement: Observation before action is qualified beyond RM's stated triggers: he seizes Adam White before hearing him out when the news concerns his father (ch.183 · s024¶172-235), and he acts on one reply from the bound prisoner after Taeshik with no family trigger (ch.34 · s002¶2044-2120; DD §15, §48).

No rule predicts where punishment ends: he stops at Thomas Andre's surrender, Hwang Dongsoo dies and serves as a shadow, and Seo Gyu-nam's punishment and the earlier offenders' have no stated end (RM §19.10; DD §24, §45, Conditional profile).

His stated refusal to choose which memories others keep (외전 10) coexists with unrequested alteration for Kim Chul and Seo Jin-i and the sealing of Suho's memories; RM directs that the tension be modeled, not resolved (RM §7.4; DD §43, §45).

The Jeju offer for a summons-count rule and the mana display to Go Gunhee belong to the death-realm simulation (ch.218 · s027¶1157-1257), not actual history; the actual accommodation is the ch.145 headcount request (RM §5.2, State D-S; DD §33).
No motive is given for his denial to Lee Juhee or his deferral with Cha in the reset, and Juhee's retained feelings are unknown (ch.243 · s030¶1536-1559; 외전 17 · s032¶626-642; RM §7.4; DD §41).
That his early teasing of Cha is flirtation is a possible reading, not a settled one (ch.134 · s014¶1645-1654; RM §10.2).
The record does not establish a general right of a shadow to leave his service; one soldier refuses an order and Beru overrides one when defending him (DD §28).

RM's utterance-length figures come from an attribution-adjacent heuristic it calls diagnostic, which misses unattributed turns and does not normalize for scene opportunity; Cha Hae-In's sampled turns are as short as his (RM §3).
Uncorrected V1 claims in RM, including the Choi Yura, Yoo Myunghan, Beru and Bellion, Jinah melon and reset Christmas anchors, are retained as index_split pointers only (RM Locators, §24).
Durable food dislikes, music and habitual leisure beyond the located examples are not established.
No predictive probe has been run against RM, and no hand-validated dialogue corpus, full register sets or decision trees for mercy, punishment, secrecy and paternalism exist.
Performed voice and manhwa-only material, including the adolescent Suho trials, are outside this evidence set.
